Rohu.habitat: Freshwater rivers, ponds and lakes of South Asia
Rohu.diet: Herbivorous - feeds on plankton, algae and decaying plants
Rohu.fun_fact: Rohu is one of the most farmed freshwater fish in India and is a major part of Indian aquaculture.

Catla.habitat: Rivers and lakes of South Asia, mainly surface water
Catla.diet: Feeds mainly on zooplankton near the water surface
Catla.avg_size: up to 180 cm, can weigh over 45 kg
Catla.fun_fact: Catla has a large, broad head and upturned mouth, ideal for surface feeding.

Tilapia.habitat: Warm freshwater lakes, rivers, and ponds worldwide
Tilapia.fun_fact: Tilapia is one of the most widely farmed fish on Earth due to its fast growth and hardiness.

Salmon.habitat: Cold rivers and the North Atlantic Ocean; anadromous species
Salmon.conservation_status: Least Concern (wild populations declining in some regions)
Salmon.fun_fact: Salmon are famous for swimming upstream against strong currents to spawn in the river where they were born.

Tuna.habitat: Open ocean, warm and temperate seas worldwide
Tuna.avg_size: 1 - 3 m depending on species, up to 450 kg (Bluefin)
Tuna.conservation_status: Varies by species, several are Near Threatened
Tuna.fun_fact: Tuna can swim at speeds of over 70 km/h and are partially warm-blooded, unusual for fish.

Clownfish.habitat: Coral reefs in warm Indo-Pacific waters, lives among sea anemones
Clownfish.fun_fact: Clownfish are immune to the sting of the sea anemones they live in, which offers them protection from predators.

Betta.habitat: Shallow freshwater in rice paddies and slow streams of Southeast Asia
Betta.fun_fact: Male bettas are extremely territorial and are commonly known as Siamese fighting fish.

Goldfish.habitat: Freshwater ponds, lakes, and aquariums worldwide
Goldfish.avg_size: 5 - 20 cm in captivity, larger in the wild
Goldfish.fun_fact: Goldfish were first domesticated in China over a thousand years ago from wild carp.

Hilsa.habitat: Coastal waters and rivers of South Asia; anadromous species
Hilsa.diet: Feeds mainly on phytoplankton and zooplankton
Hilsa.fun_fact: Hilsa is the national fish of Bangladesh and is famous for its rich flavor.

Pomfret.habitat: Coastal marine waters of the Indo-Pacific
Pomfret.diet: Feeds on zooplankton and small jellyfish
Pomfret.fun_fact: Silver Pomfret has a distinctive flat, disc-shaped silvery body and no visible pelvic fins.

Mackerel.habitat: Cold and temperate waters of the Atlantic Ocean
Mackerel.fun_fact: Mackerel swim in large, tightly packed schools that can contain thousands of fish for protection.

Catfish.habitat: Freshwater rivers, ponds, swamps and rice fields
Catfish.diet: Omnivorous - scavenges plants, insects, small fish
Catfish.fun_fact: Some catfish species can breathe air and survive out of water for short periods by moving across land.

Guppy.habitat: Freshwater streams, originally from South America, now popular globally in aquariums
Guppy.diet: Omnivorous - algae, insect larvae, small invertebrates
Guppy.fun_fact: Guppies are livebearers, meaning they give birth to free-swimming young instead of laying eggs.

Angelfish.habitat: Slow-moving freshwater rivers of the Amazon basin
Angelfish.diet: Omnivorous - small insects, worms, plant matter
Angelfish.fun_fact: Angelfish have a distinctive flat, triangular body shape and long trailing fins.

Shark.habitat: Oceans worldwide, from shallow coastal waters to deep sea
Shark.diet: Carnivorous - fish, seals, plankton depending on species
Shark.avg_size: varies widely, 20 cm to over 12 m (Whale Shark)
Shark.conservation_status: Many species are Vulnerable or Endangered
Shark.fun_fact: Sharks have skeletons made entirely of cartilage instead of bone.
